speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech problems. To help me understand the severity and location of the issue, have you noticed any weakness in your legs or hands, and do you have any history of back pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning. To narrow down whether this is compressing the spinal cord or affecting the brain, do you have any numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, and do you find yourself stumbling or tripping often?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C). The combination of progressive cerebellar signs (slurred speech, tremor), autonomic dysfunction (urinary incontinence, orthostatic hypotension), and parkinsonian features (rigidity, gait difficulty) is highly specific for this condition.
